package_info.why_malicious: The provided report is a sector-wide threat analysis and does not describe any specific malicious software package or code. Instead, it outlines attack trends, techniques, and risks relevant to the retail sector, such as ransomware, phishing, credential theft, and third-party compromise. No individual package or codebase is identified as malicious.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing emails targeting retail employees or customers
Credential stuffing attacks against e-commerce platforms
Deployment of web shells on compromised retail servers
Exfiltration of PII or employee data
file_indicators: Unexpected web shell files on e-commerce servers (e.g., .php, .asp, .jsp in upload directories)
Unusual scripts or binaries in third-party vendor integration points
Files containing large dumps of PII or credentials
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known ransomware command-and-control domains
Connections to suspicious or newly registered domains (especially during post-compromise stages)
Unusual traffic to file-sharing or pastebin services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for phishing attempts targeting employees and customers, especially those spoofing well-known retail brands. Detect credential stuffing by identifying repeated failed logins from the same IP or user agent. Scan for web shells or unauthorized scripts on e-commerce servers. Watch for large outbound data transfers or connections to known malicious infrastructure. Audit third-party integrations for anomalous behavior, and monitor for ransomware indicators such as mass file encryption or ransom notes.
